source_text.body:
Build a Home Assistant expert agent from your config
A user made a Gem/agent loaded with their entities and configuration YAML to help generate working smart home code.
·
Jan 1, 2026
Done with
GE
Gemini
What they did
One commenter built a Gemini Gem as a Home Assistant expert by uploading their entities list, configuration YAML, and setup details into the agent’s knowledge base. They used it to generate ESPHome and Home Assistant code, then pasted compiler errors back into chat so the agent could revise the code until it worked; for small setups they just copy-pasted entities, and suggested larger lists could be uploaded as a document.
How it went
They said it got the code working and let them finish in about a day, much faster than doing it alone. They also noted there were compile hiccups, old repositories, and missed details that needed follow-up prompts or error-driven fixes.
Worth knowing
The main catch was context: the agent worked better after loading entities, config YAML, setup details, and even saved prompt wording for reuse.
Try it yourself
with
Gemini
Copy prompt
Act as a Home Assistant expert using the entities and configuration YAML I'm pasting here: [paste entity list and relevant YAML]. I want an automation that does [describe goal, e.g. turn on hall lights at sunset when someone is home]. Write working YAML using only my real entity names, explain where each piece goes, and flag anything you're unsure about so I can check it before saving.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/homeassistant/comments/1q3winh/writing_yaml_with_chatgpt_claude
